data.description:

The Case For, And The Case Against SES AI Back Then

The shares cost US$1.8 at the start of the period. Anyone looking at SES AI then had to decide whether electrification trends and its AI battery platform could justify paying that upfront.

On the bullish side, one scenario pointed to a Fair Value of US$2, a price implied by forecasts that assumed revenue growth of 176.1% a year and profit margins reaching 13.6% within about three years.

The more cautious view saw Fair Value at US$1.33 based on projected 160.0% annual revenue growth, 10.0% margins, and the risk that heavy customer concentration could hit those targets.

What The Results Changed For The SES AI Thesis

The most concrete news was that SES AI reaffirmed its 2026 revenue guidance of US$30 million to US$35 million and signed multiyear ESS and drone related contracts, which supported the bullish focus on multiple business lines. At the same time, class action filings over alleged revenue misstatements and Q3 2026 figures showing revenue down while the loss narrowed, with net margin still at -201.6%, kept the profitability part of the optimistic case unproven. Overall, the evidence cut both ways.

The key lesson is about what to test first. When a story hangs on rapid revenue compounding and a fast swing to double digit margins, you can track that by watching reported top line, net income and net margin each quarter against the original growth and profitability assumptions that justified the Fair Value range.

SES AI Today, And What The Price Really Reflects

Today SES AI trades at US$0.36, with the story now anchored less to hype and more to whether operations can climb out of heavy losses. Revenue in Q3 2026 was US$6.64 million compared with US$7.118 million a year earlier, while the loss narrowed and net margin improved from very deep negative territory to -201.6%.

That mix of weaker sales and better profitability raises one question: Has sentiment fallen further than the earnings power, especially if the valuation CTA assumptions around future margins still look aggressive?

The AI Gigafactory Northern consortium looks most relevant for Nokia Oyj because it links directly to AI infrastructure demand in Europe and leans on Nokia’s strength in secure connectivity. data.title: ALTEOGEN (KOSDAQ:196170) Posted Healthy Earnings But There Are Some Other Factors To Be Aware Of
data.description:
Despite posting some strong earnings, the market for ALTEOGEN Inc.'s (KOSDAQ:196170) stock hasn't moved much. We did some digging, and we found some concerning factors in the details.

This technology could replace computers: discover the 20 stocks are working to make quantum computing a reality.

Zooming In On ALTEOGEN's Earnings

One key financial ratio used to measure how well a company converts its profit to free cash flow (FCF) is the accrual ratio. In plain english, this ratio subtracts FCF from net profit, and divides that number by the company's average operating assets over that period. You could think of the accrual ratio from cashflow as the 'non-FCF profit ratio'.

As a result, a negative accrual ratio is a positive for the company, and a positive accrual ratio is a negative. While it's not a problem to have a positive accrual ratio, indicating a certain level of non-cash profits, a high accrual ratio is arguably a bad thing, because it indicates paper profits are not matched by cash flow. That's because some academic studies have suggested that high accruals ratios tend to lead to lower profit or less profit growth.

Over the twelve months to September 2026, ALTEOGEN recorded an accrual ratio of 0.54. That means it didn't generate anywhere near enough free cash flow to match its profit. As a general rule, that bodes poorly for future profitability. In fact, it had free cash flow of ₩115b in the last year, which was a lot less than its statutory profit of ₩212.3b. We note, however, that ALTEOGEN grew its free cash flow over the last year.
